Subject: Hyperscaler interop scorecard & next tests — recap

Hi Alyssa / Tom —

Thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we hand this off to engineering for the side-by-side tests. I’ve attached a lightweight scorecard and a starter test matrix for the scenarios we discussed.

Summary of customer priorities (from the call):
- Deterministic structured outputs for order reconciliation (strong requirement)
- Reliable function/tool-calling for real-time inventory actions (must support async callbacks)
- Sub-100ms streaming latency for short tokens on 1–2k qps (target for checkout UX)
- Clear fallback behavior and cost delta vs your current hyperscaler endpoints

What Redwood can do next (proposed):
1) Run three controlled parity tests we outlined in the matrix — focus on function-calls, structured JSON schema validation, and streaming tail latency.
2) Provide a per-test performance & delta report (latency p50/p95, token cost estimate, failure modes) and a short demo video of the streaming behavior.
3) Share a canonical prompt + eval harness you can run to reproduce results in your environment.

Requested from FastRetail (please confirm):
- Which 2 SKUs and 1 checkout flow we should use for the structured-output test?
- Are we OK with using a masked dataset (anonymized IDs) for replication?

Attachments: interop_scorecard_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB), fastretail-test-matrix.xlsx (Excel, 45KB)

Next meeting: propose Tue 21 Jul (30m) to review initial results and decide on scale tests. If you want the engineering deep-dive first, we can schedule 60m.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

Jordan —

Appreciate the summary and the attachments. Quick answers below: 

- SKUs: use SKU-RT-201 and SKU-RT-402 for the structured-output test (they exercise optional fields).
- Checkout flow: the express checkout that skips loyalty is the most time-sensitive.
- Data: masked/anonymized dataset is fine — we’ll provide a CSV with mapped IDs and test payloads.

Two clarifying questions: 
1) For function/tool-calling you mentioned "async callbacks" — can Redwood surface an event when a function completes so our backend can reconcile? If so, can you document retry behavior?
2) For streaming latency, we run regional traffic from us-west-2. Can you confirm whether Redwood will run the parity test from the same region or from your central infra? Latency numbers are only useful if region matches.

Tom — FYI on the test matrix. We want to include the hyperscaler we're currently evaluating (InfraOps), so please let us know if you want to own the InfraOps run on your side or have Redwood run it.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Director, Product — FastRetail
alyssa@fastretail.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Hyperscaler interop scorecard & next tests — recap

Alyssa — quick technical clarifications below (copying Evelyn for rollout planning):

> For function/tool-calling you mentioned "async callbacks" — can Redwood surface an event when a function completes so our backend can reconcile? If so, can you document retry behavior?

Yes — Redwood supports both synchronous function/tool-calls (direct response with payload) and an async invocation mode where the runtime emits a delivery event to a webhook you specify. Behavior:
- Delivery guarantees: at-least-once delivery with idempotency keys included in the webhook payload.
- Retries: exponential backoff up to 5 attempts by default; we include reason codes and a delivery attempt count in the payload.
- Failure modes: if all retries fail we persist an audit event in the customer audit logs and trigger an operator alert per your SLA.

> For streaming latency, we run regional traffic from us-west-2. Can you confirm whether Redwood will run the parity test from the same region or from your central infra?

We can run both: Redwood Hosted in us-west-2 (same infra we use for production parity tests) and a Redwood Dedicated replica if you prefer isolated runs. For fairness vs InfraOps, we recommend both parties run the test from the same VM image in us-west-2; our matrix includes an instruction to pin region + model variant.

Proposed concrete next actions (technical):
- FastRetail: upload masked CSV and sample checkout payloads to the shared drive by Fri 17 Jul EOD.
- FastRetail / InfraOps: confirm who will execute the InfraOps side of the parity run (Tom?)
- Redwood: run 3 parity scenarios in us-west-2 within 48h of files arriving and share raw logs + structured evals.

Attaching a short appendix with webhook payload example and idempotency header names in the Drive doc.

—Karthik
